Md Lokman Karim, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner.

Vs

full_judgment:
Respondent No. 2, Sonali Bank Limited, WAPDA Bhaban Branch, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka (hereinafter stated as the Bank), as plaintiff, on 17-2-1990 filed Dewani Mokaddama No. 52 of 1990 before Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 1, Dhaka for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 1,32,42,362 against Mofiz Ahmed, Bashir Ahmed (predecessor of respondents No. 4-7 and predecessor of petitioner and respondent No. 9 and 10 respectively) and others. Then, after promulgation of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 1990, the suit was transferred and re-number as Title Suit No. 305 of 1991 before the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka (shortly, the Adalat). Eventually, the suit was decreed exparte by judgment and decree dated 5-10-1992 (preliminary decree signed on 13-1-1993). Judgment debtors having failed to pay the decreetal dues the Bank filed Dewani Decree Jari Case No. 15 of 1993 before the Adalat. During continuation of the said execution case, on 23-10-1997, the judgment-debtor-Bashir Ahmed had died leaving behind the petitioner and respondents No. 8 to 10 as his heirs The Judgment-debtor-Mofiz Ahmed also died on 13-10-1999 leaving behind respondents No. 3-7 as his heirs. Bashir Ahmed i.e the predecessor of the petitioner never mortgaged his properties to the Bank but his properties were shown in the schedule of the plaint at serial Nos. 6, 7, 12 & 13 by the Bank. The Bank was fully well aware about the death of the Judgment debtors No. 3 and 4 from the report of process server. But the Bank arranged auction sale of the mortgaged properties by publishing auction notice in connivance with respondents Nos. 3-7. Respondents Nos. 3-7 had purchased the plaint schedule properties in auction in the benami of alleged auction purchaser, showing the value of the properties at its purchased price long before. After arranging above fraudulent auction without informing the same to the petitioner and other heirs of the deceased Bashir Ahmed, they created a deed of purchase from the alleged auction purchaser. After completing the said acts, they filed an application for correction of Boinama of Plot No. 59 as mentioned at serial No. 6 of the Boinama as Plot No. 51 (hereinafter stated as the Property) without praying for amendment of judgment and preliminary decree, application for execution of decree, proclamation of sale, etc. The learned Judge of the Adalat directed the judgment-debtor-applicants to serve the copy of the application to contesting parties. But without serving the copy upon the learned Advocate for the petitioner by showing fake signatures of some of the judgment-debtors they pressed the application. Whereupon, the learned Judge of the Adalat unlawfully passed the impugned order for correction of Boinama by inserting the Property i.e. Plot No. 51 in place of Plot No. 59, beyond his jurisdiction. Prior to that, the petitioner had filed an application on 30-4-2014 under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (shortly, the Code) read with section 57 of the Artha Kin Adalat Ain, 2003 (briefly, the Ain) for modification of previous order No. 115 dated 17-11-2008 passed in the execution case. Hearing of the said application was complete on 16-4-2015 by the Adalat and 5-5-2015 was fixed for passing order on that application of the petitioner. The petitioner filed hazira on that date but was absent from the Adalat. The learned Judge without passing order on the petitioner's application passed the impugned order for correction of the Boinama on the application of the applicant-judgment-debtors dated 29-4-2015 illegally. Hence, this writ petition. 

 3. Respondent No. 2 the Bank contested the Rule by filing an affidavit in opposition supporting the impugned order contending, inter alia, that late Bashir Ahmed father of the petitioner had mortgaged the properties mentioned in schedule Kha of the plaint. Bashir Ahmed had died long after the decree. Due to clerical error, the Adalat officials incorrectly mentioned Plot No. 59 instead of Plot No. 51 in the certified copy of the Judgment and decree. Due to the said mistake Plot No. 59 was written instead of Plot No. 51 at serial No. 6 by the Bank in the execution application and the proclamation of sale. In the Boinama (sale certificate) also Plot No. 59 was mentioned in place of Plot No. 51. Therefore, the learned Judge of the Adalat legally and correctly allowed amendment of Boinama by the impugned order No. 94 dated 5-5-2015. The Property has been handed over to the auction purchaser upon confirmation of auction sale. In the circumstances, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 4. Respondent No. 6, Rakib Ahmed contested the Rule supporting the impugned order contending, inter alia, that the auction sale was confirmed long before; that due to typing error Plot No. 59 was mentioned in the Boinama in place of Plot No. 51. So, the learned Judge of the Adalat legally passed the impugned order for correction of the Boinama; that the writ petition misconceived, not maintainable and the Rule is thus, liable to be discharged. 

 (4) from application of the execution case and the proclamation of sale, which was published in the daily Bangla Bazar on 9-6-2003, it is evident that the Plot No. 59 is written at serial No.6 and Plot No. 51 was not at all mentioned either in the application for execution of decree or in the proclamation of sale; 

 (5) in the circumstances there is no scope to correct the Bionama (sale certificate) by the Adalat. Therefore, the impugned order of correction of the Boinama suffers from legal infirmity and, as such, liable to be struck down; 

 7. Ms. Hosneara Begum, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 2 takes us through the affidavit in opposition and frankly concedes that in the certified copy of the decree the plot number was mentioned as 59 instead of Plot No. 51. Therefore, execution case filed by the Bank mentioning Plot No.59 at serial No. 6 of the schedule of the execution case as well as in the proclamation of sale. 

 9. Mr Md Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate for respondent No. 6, Rakib Ahmed, son of late Judgment-debtor-Mofiz Ahmed, takes us through the affidavit-in-opposition and frankly concedes that after auction sale of the mortgaged properties, being a Judgment debtor, respondent No.6 and respondents No.7 and 8 had purchased auction sold properties of the late Bashir Ahmed from the auction purchaser. However, he submits that mentioning Plot No. 59 in place of Plot No. 51 at serial No. 6 of the execution case as well as in the proclamation of sale was a simple typing error. Therefore, the impugned order allowing the application for correction of the Plot number by the Adalat is lawful. 

 13. From the application filed by the Judgment-debtors, it appears that it was for correction of CS, SA Plot No. 51 in place of Plot No. 50 in the Boinama i.e. the sale certificate. Admittedly, neither the execution application nor the proclamation of sale is corrected till date. 

 From order No. 15 dated 13-2-2011 it reveals that after confirmation of sale the decree-holder filed an application for correction of the schedule of the sale certificate by inserting BS plot Nos. 1271, 1272 and 1273 in place of BS Plot Nos. 1171, 1172 and 1172 and accordingly the Adalat directed to correct the plot numbers as prayed by the decree-holder. It is apparent on the face of the record the decree-holder got the plot numbers of the property correct which was sold in execution of the decree after the confirmation of the sale which is enough to bring the matter within the mischief of Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting-aside auction sale on the ground of material irregularity. It also appears that the judgment-debtor filed an application for setting-aside the auction sale by misquoting section 33(2) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain which should have been filed under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure as observed by the Adalat. In the decision of Antibiotics Stores vs Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat reported in 55 DLR (AD) 13 = 8 BLD (AD) 8 our apex Court held: 

 'In the present case the impugned order has been passed in the execution proceeding and the petitioner could avail the provision of Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure in setting-aside the auction sale on ground of material irregularity find fraud alleged by any of the party to the execution proceeding arising out of judgment and decree passed under the Ain as the same could have been adequately dealt with under the said provision, and in the facts and circumstances of the instant case the writ jurisdiction's not maintainable for deciding the question of fraud and material irregularity in publishing and conducting the sale, which are essentially a question of fact to be determined on evidence and could not be conveniently dealt with in writ jurisdiction. Reference in this regard may be made in the case of Sarder Jan-e-Alam vs Arab Bangladesh Bank Ltd. reported in 4 BLC (AD) 178." 

 15. In view of the above, we are of the opinion that the impugned order for correction of Plot No. 51 in place of Plot No. 59 in the Boinama (sale certificate) without correction of the application for execution of decree and proclamation of sale suffers from legal infirmity. It is apparent on the face of the record that some of the judgment-debtors who are heirs of Mofiz Ahmed had purchased properties of late Bashir Ahmed from the alleged auction purchaser and subsequently, filed the application for correction of plot number of a plot after confirmation of the sale, which is enough to bring the matter under the mischief of Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code for setting-aside auction sale on the ground of material irregularity and fraud. An application is also pending for modification of the previous order of the Adalat rejecting an application under Order XXI, rule 90 of the Code without treating it as a miscellaneous case and without taking evidence. 

 16. In the above scenario, the impugned order of correction without disposal of the petitioner's application first cannot be said to be lawful.
